stem: If a child presents with features belonging to different asthma severity categories, how should their overall severity be determined?

options.text: By the average of all observed features.
By the feature indicating the highest or worst severity.
By the category that contains the majority of the features.
By the child's baseline developmental status only.

explanation: To ensure patient safety, the presence of even a single high-risk feature mandates categorization into the more severe group.
rationale: Consider how you would manage a patient who appears stable but has one life-threatening indicator.

optionExplanations.A: Averaging symptoms would underestimate the clinical risk associated with the most dangerous features.
optionExplanations.B: To ensure patient safety, the presence of even a single high-risk feature mandates categorization into the more severe group.
optionExplanations.C: Safety protocols require prioritizing the most severe individual clinical indicator over a majority of milder ones.
optionExplanations.D: While developmental status helps interpret symptoms like speech ability, the clinical features of the acute episode determine the severity category.
